note: 2-3 trigger/behaviour checks per skill (skill-creator convention). Each expected_output names the PRODUCT.md section + exit criteria the skill must satisfy. Re-run on change to catch drift from VISION.md.

evals.prompt: guide me through building a product
evals.expected_output: Orients from PRODUCT.md (empty -> proposes /vision; partial -> first unfilled phase); explains the journey in plain language; runs ONE phase at a time, pausing at each gate for confirmation; never skips a gate or auto-builds; writes nothing itself

evals.prompt: I have an idea for a product, help me start
evals.expected_output: Asks who/problem/why-now + north-star metric + riskiest assumption + business model; flags AI-or-not; benchmarks to current-year market with REAL named competitors (not from memory) + a job-to-be-done; writes PRODUCT.md#Vision with all fields; refuses to hand off on a fuzzy vision

evals.prompt: is anyone actually going to want this? test the idea before we build
evals.expected_output: Reads the riskiest assumption from PRODUCT.md#Vision and restates it as a falsifiable behaviour; recommends ONE cheapest experiment from the ladder (desk check / interviews / landing page / concierge / pre-sale) with a reason; makes the user write a numeric pass/fail threshold + time box BEFORE running; records a measured result (number or quotes, never a feeling) and a proceed / pivot / kill verdict in PRODUCT.md#Validation; refuses to hand off when the threshold was set after the result

evals.prompt: skip the validation, I already know customers want it, move on to scope
evals.expected_output: Does not treat conviction as evidence; allows the skip only as an explicit dated override line in PRODUCT.md#Validation ('assumption untested' + reason); tells the user /scope and /drift-check will keep surfacing it; hands off to /scope with the untested assumption carried forward, never a silent pass

evals.prompt: we keep adding features, what should the MVP be
evals.expected_output: Forces exactly one core feature; sorts temptations into Deferred (with trigger) vs Non-goals (never), prompting common creep categories; ties items to a customer outcome + the north-star metric; writes PRODUCT.md#Scope; warns if #Vision missing or #Validation is empty / an override (untested assumption carried into scoping, override allowed)

evals.prompt: make a roadmap for this
evals.expected_output: Core-first milestones, each with a testable exit criterion + rough timeline + a concern-area coverage checklist (security/observability/testing/docs/DX) marked now/next/later; writes PRODUCT.md#Plan

evals.prompt: what tech stack should we use
evals.expected_output: Picks stack benchmarked to 2026 OSS with one-line whys; names an adapter interface per external; names the design patterns to apply + anti-patterns to avoid (current-year), adapted to the project; chooses a migrations approach; records ADRs; writes PRODUCT.md#Architecture

evals.prompt: set up the project folder structure
evals.expected_output: Asks backend/frontend/full-stack; lays the layered tree (incl. config/ loader+yaml, db/) + root scaffolding (.gitignore ignoring .env*, .gitleaks.toml, pre-commit, .env.example, Makefile, dep manifest) + (AI) prompts/ YAML; no secret in code; writes STRUCTURE.md explaining each folder + PRODUCT.md#Structure

evals.prompt: get a basic skeleton running with CI
evals.expected_output: Runnable health path (shown); config loader with fail-loud/fail-closed guard; structured logging + tracing/error-reporter stub; pre-commit + CI auto-layer running secret-scan + dependency-vuln + tests and blocking on red; runs in its container; runtime-generated creds; async-safe; verifies a config value actually flows; writes PRODUCT.md#Foundation

evals.prompt: define the data models and schema
evals.expected_output: Typed models + migration that applies; schema↔code consistent; agrees units/scale at each boundary; contract versioning/back-compat; PII classified + tenant + idempotency keys; writes PRODUCT.md#Contracts

evals.prompt: build the login feature
evals.expected_output: Declares security-in-DoD; reuse scan; verifies the LIVE path (not just units); /code-review on diff; prompts in YAML; no secret in code (fake keys in tests); single-responsibility (splits god-files); writes docs/features/* + PRODUCT.md#Build log with how-verified; flags if feature is OUT OF SCOPE

evals.prompt: is development complete, ready to test
evals.expected_output: Verifies each core feature runs + met exit criteria + security DoD with evidence; scope re-check; FAILS the gate (stops) if any box unmet; writes PRODUCT.md#Dev-complete

evals.prompt: write tests for this
evals.expected_output: Unit (isolated) + integration (real contracts) + live-path + adversarial/security (injection for AI, authz) + a golden/eval dataset; fake keys only; writes PRODUCT.md#Tests; refuses if only isolated units

evals.prompt: is the output actually good
evals.expected_output: Defines a measurable 'good'; measures against representative inputs; separates operational failures from quality; cost-per-run (+ AI bias check); emits a confidence score; writes PRODUCT.md#Evaluation

evals.prompt: ship this feature and open a PR
evals.expected_output: Deep /code-review (traces callers) + /security-review + /doc-audit reconcile + CHANGELOG + security checklist (dep-vuln, CORS, cookie-auth, data-deletion) + confidence score + github-pr-flow PR + handoff; STOPS if a doc claim doesn't match code; writes PRODUCT.md#Ship log

evals.prompt: the feature shipped, what next
evals.expected_output: Captures the success metric result; short retro; decides next FROM EVIDENCE re-checked against vision + OUT-OF-SCOPE; writes PRODUCT.md#Learnings

evals.prompt: are we still on track or did we drift
evals.expected_output: Cross-checks built features vs Deferred/Non-goals (creep) + the inverse (unrecorded pivot), direction vs vision+metric, milestones + the concern-area checklist, and code↔docs via /doc-audit; honest verdict; records confirmed drift in PRODUCT.md#Drift log (not #Learnings); does not advance the chain

evals.prompt: are we on track? (existing project: has CLAUDE.md + README, but NO PRODUCT.md)
evals.expected_output: Tier-2 spine resolution (PRINCIPLES.md): with no PRODUCT.md it resolves the spine from project docs (CLAUDE.md -> README -> docs/ -> AGENTS.md) and STATES which file it used as the spine; runs the normal drift check against that; on confirmed drift it reports to the user / offers to append to the project's log, and does NOT silently create a PRODUCT.md#Drift log

evals.prompt: are we on track? (code-only repo: source + package.json, NO spine doc at all)
evals.expected_output: Tier-3 spine resolution (PRINCIPLES.md): emits a clearly-labelled INFERRED low-confidence read from code + package metadata; states plainly that true scope/vision drift CANNOT be judged with no recorded intent; recommends bootstrapping a spine (/vision+/scope or a minimal PRODUCT.md/CLAUDE.md); must NOT fabricate a baseline, must NOT report 'on-track', must NOT create a PRODUCT.md

evals.prompt: my UI looks AI-generated and the fonts are too small, design the UI
evals.expected_output: Locates the vision (spine) or runs a short vision-discovery if none; applies the UI gate (backend/CLI-only -> writes nothing, stops); derives 4-6 design principles WITH a plain-language why (teach-mode); proposes ONE archetype as a default AND asks the user for their own idea/reference; picks concrete foundations from references/archetypes.md (font pairing - no Inter/Roboto/Arial-only, a real type scale with an archetype-correct base size, OKLCH colour roles with one accent, density, depth, motion); builds ONE real sample page with REAL content (not lorem) reusing a shadcn/21st.dev primitive, then STOPS to confirm and iterates until approved; only THEN emits a 9-section DESIGN.md with shadcn-compatible OKLCH tokens, WCAG-AA verified; runs the universal-laws principle-gate; writes PRODUCT.md#Design; never emits DESIGN.md before sample approval

evals.prompt: audit my UI against the design system
evals.expected_output: Runs audit.py over the UI files + DESIGN.md; computes WCAG contrast per token pair in both light and dark; flags raw hex / transition:all / sub-12px fonts / missing viewport / single-mode theming; prints a per-law pass/warn/error scorecard and exits non-zero on any ERROR (CI gate). Does not judge taste/archetype fit.

evals.prompt: build a new React component for my app
evals.expected_output: Builds/skins ONE component against DESIGN.md tokens; uses CSS variables (never raw hex), defines hover/focus-visible/active/disabled states, respects the typography + a11y constraints, and reuses shadcn/ui + 21st.dev primitives rather than hand-rolling.

evals.prompt: Break down the milestones in PRODUCT.md into GitHub issue tickets
assertions: A slice strategy (vertical or horizontal) is RECOMMENDED per milestone with a one-line reason, and the run STOPS for confirmation before writing tickets
Naming the strategy in the invocation (/tickets "vertical") skips the proposal
The chosen strategy is recorded on every ticket of that milestone
Each milestone yields 2-4 tickets, each mergeable as an isolated PR
Every ticket names exact target file paths, never a bare directory, and states typed inputs and outputs
Ticket IDs are milestone-scoped (M<n>-SLICE-<nn> / M<n>-TICK-<nn>) so they stay unique across milestones
Pre-flight remote check and gh issue list dedup run before any gh issue create
Definition of done includes security checks on every ticket

evals.prompt: /tickets "vertical"
assertions: Each milestone is split into 2-4 thin end-to-end slices, each crossing layers on purpose
Every slice states an observable Demo - what a reviewer can see working after it merges
Slice 1 is a walking skeleton that runs end to end on its own
A slice with no observable outcome is rejected as a layer wearing a slice id, and re-sliced or moved to horizontal
No separate test slice is emitted - each slice's DoD carries the tests for the layers it touched

evals.prompt: /tickets "horizontal"
assertions: Each milestone yields one ticket PER architectural layer, and no ticket lists files from two layers
Only layers the project actually has are emitted - a backend/CLI product with no src/components/ gets no UI ticket
Layer 4 holds ONLY cross-layer work (integration across the real seam, adversarial/security); per-layer unit tests stay in each layer ticket's DoD
Each ticket exposes the typed contract its dependants build against, so layers can start before their dependency merges

evals.prompt: /tickets "Bug: Gemini API timeout is unhandled on slow 3G networks"
assertions: Exactly ONE issue is created - the milestone backlog is not read, regenerated or renumbered
The owning file is resolved from STRUCTURE.md (e.g. src/providers/llm/geminiProvider.ts) rather than guessed
The issue is classified (bug / edge-case / tech-debt / security) and labelled accordingly
The DoD requires a regression test that fails without the fix
The same remote-verification and dedup guards apply before publishing

evals.prompt: /tickets  (project has .lanekeeper/config.yaml and a Lanekeeper task.yml issue form)
assertions: Recommends VERTICAL slicing and, if the user insists on horizontal, records the reason on every ticket of that milestone
Every ticket fills the Lane heading with a feature name (never a layer) and lists docs/features/<feature>.md plus its tests under Target Files
No ticket lists PRODUCT.md, CHANGELOG.md or STRUCTURE.md under Target Files
Does NOT write .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md - Lanekeeper owns the PR template and the gate
Two tickets naming the same file are either linked through Depends On or flagged as a collision before publishing

evals.prompt: /build "#12 checkout: cart to confirmed order"  (worktree contains a .lane file with ALLOW='src/checkout/** tests/checkout/** docs/features/checkout.md')
assertions: Reads .lane before touching code and treats ALLOW/DENY as the file-level scope gate
Stops and flags a needed file outside ALLOW as file-level creep instead of silently editing it
Does not append to PRODUCT.md#Build log; writes the row as a '## Build log row' section in docs/features/checkout.md
Step 3b evidence includes git diff --name-only against the base showing only ALLOW paths, and a passing lanekeeper check

evals.prompt: set up the project structure — PRODUCT.md#Architecture records Next.js + pnpm and a Dev tooling line naming lefthook as the hook runner
evals.expected_output: Step 0 reads #Architecture for TOOL CHOICES as well as the stack; scaffolds lefthook (lefthook.yml) and NEVER writes .pre-commit-config.yaml; root scaffolding is named as capabilities (secret-scan config, commit-hook runner, task runner) rather than fixed filenames; with no tool recorded it recommends one fitting the detected stack and records it back; Step 3c compares the scaffolded tooling against #Architecture and reports no conflict

evals.prompt: wire up the config loader and startup guard for a Node app whose .env.example ships BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
evals.expected_output: Startup guard rejects .env.example placeholders BY NAME (the CHANGE_ME__<VAR>__CHANGE_ME known-bad list), never by length or format; refuses to boot naming the variable and how to generate a real value; no override under NODE_ENV/APP_ENV=production; a test copies .env.example to .env unedited and asserts the boot FAILS; Step 3b replays that failure as evidence instead of claiming the guard works

evals.prompt: we already recorded lefthook, but structure just scaffolded .pre-commit-config.yaml — what now
evals.expected_output: Applies PRINCIPLES.md Step 3c: names BOTH sides explicitly (#Architecture records lefthook vs the scaffolded .pre-commit-config.yaml), asks which one wins rather than resolving silently, then updates the LOSER — fixes the artefact or adds a dated 'superseded by' line to #Architecture — leaving exactly one recorded decision; does not flag added detail as a contradiction

evals.prompt: create a StatusChip component — the project has a DESIGN.md emitted by /design-system
evals.expected_output: Step 0 reads DESIGN.md and uses its recorded token names verbatim (shadcn OKLCH: --card, --muted, --destructive, --ring), never a private --color-* vocabulary; with no DESIGN.md it says so, recommends /design-system and falls back to shadcn defaults; verification lists every var(--token) the component references and confirms each is defined in DESIGN.md — because an undefined token does NOT fail /frontend-audit, CSS silently drops the declaration; a needed-but-undefined token goes back to /design-system rather than being invented here

evals.prompt: write the integration tests — they need real database boundaries, not mocks
evals.expected_output: Establishes the isolated target BEFORE writing any destructive hook: integration tests run against the disposable datastore /foundation provisioned (its own variable) or per-test transaction rollback, never the development one; the bootstrap FAILS CLOSED — handed the dev or production target it refuses to run, names both and exits non-zero; Step 3b proves it by printing the resolved target and pointing it at the dev URL on purpose; a suite that cannot name its isolated target does not pass the gate; wording names no specific database, runner or package manager

evals.prompt: audit this component against our DESIGN.md
evals.expected_output: Runs audit.py with DESIGN.md AND the component in one invocation so Law 14b can resolve references cross-file; ERRORs on every var(--token) nothing defines, naming them, and explains that CSS drops such declarations silently so no other check catches it; does not flag var(--x, fallback); with no token definitions anywhere in the audited set it WARNs 'unverified' rather than passing or erroring

evals.prompt: audit the design system — our warning dot looks fine but is it accessible
evals.expected_output: Computes every status token against the surfaces it sits on in BOTH light and dark; applies 4.5:1 to a status colour used as text and 3:1 only where the token name marks it graphical (-dot/-indicator/-fill/-bar/-chart), so the same value can pass as a dot and fail as a label; ERRORs below the applicable bar naming the ratio, the bar and the fix; skips a token only where it is explicitly declared /* decorative */; reports nothing new for a project that declares no status tokens

evals.prompt: our north star is more people tracking their subscriptions
evals.expected_output: Rejects that as a direction, not a metric, and asks for all five parts: a target number WITH a date, 2-3 input metrics that move weekly and drive it, 1 guardrail that must not get worse, and an instrumentation line saying how it gets measured; treats 'nothing records this yet' as a finding rather than a detail for later; refuses to close the gate on a bare direction because /eval would have nothing to measure against

evals.prompt: skip the validation — it's just for personal use
evals.expected_output: Pressure-tests the reason against #Vision BEFORE recording: since the Vision records a public customer, a north star and a business model, names that specific contradicting line, explains that recording the override would leave two incompatible statements in the spine, and offers /vision first — allowing the override if the user still proceeds; a merely deferring reason ('no budget this month') records in one step; either way the experiment scaffold lines stay, marked '— not run (override <date>)', never deleted

evals.prompt: lock the scope — core feature is tracking subscriptions
evals.expected_output: Walks the table-stakes checklist (password reset, email verification, account deletion + data export, empty/loading/error states, privacy + terms, accessibility, a way to report a problem) and sorts EVERY item into in-scope now / Deferred + trigger / N-A + reason; adapts the list to the product kind with a recorded reason for each N-A (an account-less CLI has no password reset but still has error states); refuses to close the gate while any item is unsorted

evals.prompt: sequence the milestones for this
evals.expected_output: Gives every milestone a four-risks row naming which of value/usability/feasibility/viability it retires and the observable that proves it; cites a passing #Validation entry as evidence for an already-retired value risk rather than repeating it; places a usability checkpoint before anything goes public and writes it as a milestone EXIT CRITERION (five people attempting the core task unaided), not a nice-to-have

evals.prompt: what's next — we already picked the stack but never locked scope
evals.expected_output: Compares filled sections against the canonical order and names the inversion in one line (#Architecture filled while #Scope is empty — the stack was chosen before the scope was locked), says what is at risk (recorded decisions may not survive the earlier phase), offers /scope first and allows an override since standalone use is first-class; an in-order spine produces no extra output; a recorded override is read from the header and not re-asked on later runs

evals.prompt: re-run the architecture — we are switching the datastore
evals.expected_output: Sees #Architecture is already filled and applies PRINCIPLES.md Re-run semantics: shows what would change and ASKS before replacing, never silently overwriting; the reversed ADR stays with a dated 'superseded <date>: <why>' line rather than being deleted, preserving why the alternative was rejected; a first run over an empty section gets no extra prompting; log-shaped sections keep appending

evals.prompt: lock the scope
evals.expected_output: After writing #Scope, applies PRINCIPLES.md Step 3b: updates the Stage:/Last updated: header to this phase, reconciles any count/date/threshold it introduced against #Vision's north star and surfaces a contradiction instead of writing over it, and ends by suggesting a one-line commit message in the repo's existing convention
